chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjaj, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Mu'awiyyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked: A man stands in prayer, then looks after he has finished and sees that he has deviated from the Qibla to the right or left. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His prayer is valid, and whatever is between the East and the West is a Qibla.'
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Regarding a man who prayed facing away from the Qibla, and he knew while still in prayer before finishing it: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was facing somewhere between the East and the West, let him turn his face to the Qibla when he knows [the direction]. And if he was facing the back of the Qibla, let him cut off [the prayer], then turn his face to the Qibla, then commence the prayer anew.'
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, said:

I wrote to 'Abdullah ibn Sinan (peace be upon him): A man prays on a cloudy day in an open field of land and does not know the Qibla, so he prays until when he finishes his prayer the sun appears, and he finds he has prayed facing away from the Qibla. Should he consider his prayer valid or repeat it? He wrote: 'He repeats it, as long as the time has not passed. Did he not know that Allah says, and His word is true: "So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah."'

key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.دُبُرِ الْقِبْلَة: The back of the Qibla (facing directly opposite to it)
key_terms.فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ الل: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah (Quran 2:115)
key_terms.فَلَاة: An open, empty field or plain
key_terms.مَا بَيْنَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَ الْمَغْرِبِ: Between the East and the West (a broad directional area)
key_terms.يَقْطَع: To cut off or interrupt the prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for repeating prayer if one realizes they faced the wrong Qibla direction after finishing?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance on *Ijtihad* in prayer direction, distinguishing between minor deviations where the prayer remains valid and significant misalignment requiring a restart. It further addresses the specific case of cloudy days, ruling that if the sun appears after prayer revealing a wrong direction, the prayer must be repeated unless the time has expired, citing the Quranic verse 'Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah' as evidence for the flexibility of direction in such cases.
